newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - March 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - March 17.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- TOYOTA CONSIDERS BUILDING CAR PLANT IN FRANCE

Japanese automotive giant Toyota is reported to be considering a 1 billion stg investment in constructing a car plant in northern France. News of the move, which would be part of Toyota's strategy to increase sales by 50 percent by 2000, follows comments six weeks ago by Toyota president Hiroshi Okuda that the company might change its investment strategy in Europe if the UK were to stay outside of Emu. A final decision on the plans is expected on May 10.
-- CITY WEB PLAN COULD REDUCE IT BILLS

A group of IT professionals in the City of London has joined with Andersen Consulting to propose an integrated communications system for the financial community. The project -- Port -- would operate in a similar way to the Internet, and is intended to reduce the 7 billion stg annual cost to London's financial institutions of the development, operation and maintenance of computer systems and their connections to outside networks. The scheme would incorporate existing networks built by suppliers such as Reuters, Swift, Crest and Chaps.
-- US FORCES SET TO BUY BRITISH LIGHT ARTILLERY

UK defence manufacturers BAe and VSEL will learn late on Monday which one has won a 500 million dollar (314m stg) contract from the US Pentagon to supply light field guns to the US marines. It is understood the order will be given to a UK company, despite domestic pressure to award the contract to a US company. If, as seems likely, the US army follows the lead of the Marines, the order could eventually be worth between $1 billion and $2 billion.
-- GERMANY TAKES EU TOP SPOT FOR BEEF EXPORTS

Unpublished figures compiled by the Irish Food Board show that Germany has moved ahead of France, Ireland and the Netherlands to take top spot as the biggest beef exporter in the European Union. The figures show Germany increased its exports by 3 percent last year, to a total of 440,000 tonnes. In 1995, the last full year before British beef exports were banned because of the BSE crisis, the UK exported 270,000 tonnes of beef, making it the fifth or sixth biggest exporter.
-- ANGER AT ORANGE PRICING DECISION

UK mobile phone group Orange has unexpectedly started charging premium rates to connect subscribers to a competitor's networks. The move, which does not contravene any regulations or licence conditions covering Orange, has nevertheless upset customers and infuriated rival operators. The Orange move means customers who previously were connected via a free phone number to First Telecom, a small low-cost call operator, are now charged a premium rate of 50p a minute for the connection.
-- LANG TO UNVEIL PLAN FOR AIRWAVES SELL-OFF

Trade secretary Ian Lang is expected on Monday to announce plans to raise up to 1 billion stg by privatizing the telephone airwaves. The plan, intended to show that the Conservatives still have fresh policies for the general election, involves selling parts of the radio spectrum -- used for mobile telephone and radio-paging services -- to private bidders. An aide to Lang said the measures would 'place Britain in the vanguard of the digital future'.
-- SHELL TO CONSULT PRESSURE GROUPS

Royal Dutch/Shell, the international oil company pilloried by environmentalists over plans to dispose of the Brent Spar installation at sea and for its activities in Nigeria following the execution of minority rights activist Ken Sara Wiwa, is to consult environmental and human rights groups over sensitive projects in the developing world.
-- BT/MCI FAVOURED SUITOR FOR PORTUGAL TELECOM

Concert, the global telecommunications alliance between BT and MCI of the US, has emerged as the favourite to become the foreign partner of Portugal Telecom. The two groups are reported to have been in exclusive negotiations since last week and a decision on the proposed link-up is expected as early as this week. AT&T-Unisource and Global One, the alliance led by France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom, have also submitted bids to take a stake of up to 5 percent in the Portuguese operator.
-- BELGIUM WARNS ON MERGER PLAN

The Belgian government has warned that a merger between French groups Compagnie de Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux could have serious consequences for Belgium's energy sector and, in particular, the Tractebel utility group. Suez holds a 62 percent stake in Societe Generale de Belgique, the holding company that controls Tractebel, and some observers suggest a merger with Lyonnaise des Eaux could lead to the French utility taking contracts from the Belgian energy group.
-- APPLE CUTS FAIL TO REMOVE DOUBT

Apple Computer has announced it is reduce its workforce by 30 percent in a bid to reduce annual expenses by $500m. Most of the cuts will be made in the group's marketing, research and development and manufacturing operations. "I am absolutely convinced that these decisions will put us back on the road to health," said Apple chairman and chief executive Gil Amelio. Apple also warned that its revenues for the current quarter would fall by 22 percent to 26 percent against last year to between 1.6 billion dollars and 1.7 billion dollars.
